what_this_is: The machine-readable spine of the mid-term single-repository review panel.
Every constant here is cross-checked against scripts/midtermpanel/ by
`midtermpanel.policy.assert_matches_code`, so this document and the code
cannot drift apart without a test failing. A governance file that merely
describes what the code is supposed to do is a comment with a digest.
what_this_is_not: This is NOT the trusted lane. It is not write-separated, it holds a
repository-scoped Actions secret in the repository it reviews, it rests on
no recorded operator prerequisite, and no protected environment gates it.

strict_note: `independent_verify.strict_any_refutation` is OPT-IN and OFF by default:
the reference mechanism greens on 'required approver + one corroborator'
even when a third voice refutes. Mid-term policy turns it ON, because the
plan requires that ANY valid refutation blocks. This differs from the
default on purpose and is recorded here so nobody has to infer it.

why: A manually dispatched workflow runs against a SELECTED REF, and every
checkout in the privileged workflow deliberately omits `ref:`. Under
`workflow_run` that omission is the safety property: definition and
checkout both come from the default branch. Under `workflow_dispatch`
it becomes the hazard: the checkout takes the dispatched ref, so a
dispatch against a branch carrying modified `scripts/midtermpanel`
would execute that branch's code in the jobs holding the provider key.
The runtime approval phrase authenticated the CANDIDATE under review.
It never authenticated the ref supplying the reviewer.
manual.controlled_rerun: Re-run ordinary CI on the same head — Actions UI 'Re-run all jobs', or `gh run rerun <CI_RUN_ID>`. The convenience workflow that used to do this was REMOVED: a workflow_dispatch workflow runs a branch-selected copy, so with a persistent repository secret a branch version of it could reference that secret. That is the same selected-ref hazard that removed the dispatch trigger from the privileged panel, reached through a convenience. No repository workflow with `actions: write` is needed.

statement: A repository-level Actions secret is accessible to workflows in the

change a `pull_request` workflow may be able to reference it.

policy_profiles.selected_by: MIDTERM_REVIEW_CLASS, derived by preflight.review_class_for from the pull-request number through a CLOSED rule. No caller-supplied free-form name, and no per-PR allowlist: the previous design listed pr-23/pr-25/pr-29 and would have refused every future routine pull request.
policy_profiles.honest_scope: operator-attested, not cryptographically authenticated and not write-separated.

ordinary_ci_binding.bound_to: the triggering workflow run, by exact id
ordinary_ci_binding.why: A pull-request CI run checks out a generated refs/pull/N/merge commit, so its green is evidence about a merge of the candidate with a SPECIFIC base. The previous check compared the current PR object's base to current main; both track the branch, so when main advanced they moved together and the check passed while ordinary CI had tested a combination that no longer existed.
